Senses.Explanation: Literally (公) (public / government office) + (案) (case-file, legal record). In Chan it names a recorded encounter or saying of the old masters that is taken up and set before a student. Attested uses in the corpus make the legal-office figure explicit. Zhongfeng Mingben, asked what the 'public cases' spoken of everywhere are, answers that (公案) is a figure for the case-documents of a government office (公府之案牘): (公) is the shared principle the sages all travel by, (案) is the (正文) (the authoritative text) recording how they governed; and just as a litigant who cannot settle a matter brings it to the office to be decided by the case-files, a student who has some understanding he cannot settle brings it to his teacher, who 'raises a public case to decide it' (舉公案以决之). The (碧巖錄序) (三教老人) says flatly that the two graphs are (世間法中吏牘語) — clerkly-document language of worldly law — and that reading a case is like an old clerk judging a crime in court (老吏據獄讞罪); the patriarchs 'established them as public cases and left them to instruct the monasteries' (立為公案，留示叢林). Wumen Huikai in his own preface describes taking the ancient men's public cases as a knock-on-the-door tile (敲門瓦子) to guide students according to their capacity. The (碧巖錄) preface further dates and names the genre — (甞謂祖教之書)。(謂之公案者)。(倡於唐而盛於宋) ('the books of the patriarchs' teaching, called public cases, arose in the Tang and flourished in the Song') — and enumerates (其用有三) ('their uses are three'), each by a legal simile: (如老吏據獄讞罪)。(底裏悉見)。(情欵不遺) ('like an old clerk taking up the case-file and adjudging the crime — the bottom of it fully seen, no deposition left out'); (如廷尉執法平反)。(出人於死) ('like the commandant of justice applying the law to overturn a verdict and bring a man out from death'); (如官府頒示條令)。(令人讀律知法) ('like the office promulgating statutes so that people read the code and know the law'); summing up: (具方冊)。(作案底)。(陳機境)。(為格令) ('set down in volumes, made into case-files, presenting the encounter-situations, serving as regulations'). Inside the same book, the commentary to case 98 states how the things so named arose: (未有問答)。(未有公案已前)。(還有禪道麼)。(古人事不獲已)。(對機垂示)。(後人喚作公案) ('before there were questions and answers, before there were public cases — was there a Chan way? The men of old, having no other recourse, gave pointers according to the occasion; later people called these public cases'). A Qing-era record keeps the clerk figure: (言言見諦)、(著著歸宗)，(如老吏斷獄)，(引經合律)，(一毫頭也出入不得)，(所以喚作公案) ('…like an old clerk deciding a case, citing the canon and matching the statutes, with not a hair's breadth of leeway — that is why they are called public cases', 雲溪俍亭挺禪師語錄). The word is also spoken at the sight of an arriving monk — Muzhou's (現成公案放汝三十棒) ('a ready-made case: I spare you thirty blows'), raised by Dahui (舉睦州纔見僧云。現成公案放汝三十棒, 'he raised: Muzhou, as soon as he saw a monk, said, a ready-made case — I spare you thirty blows') and in the stock litany (德山見僧入門便棒)，(臨濟見僧入門便喝)，(雪峰見僧入門便道是甚麼)，(睦州見僧便道現成公案放你三十棒) ('Deshan, seeing a monk enter the gate, struck; Linji, seeing a monk enter the gate, shouted; Xuefeng, seeing a monk enter the gate, said, what is it?; Muzhou, seeing a monk, said, a ready-made case — I spare you thirty blows'); biographies later show that line itself given to students as a saying (話) to take up (源舉現成公案放汝三十棒話，不契 — '[the monk] Yuan raised the saying 'a ready-made case — I spare you thirty blows' and did not accord'), and Zhongfeng extends the collocation: (無邊眾生各各脚跟下有一則現成公案) ('boundless beings each have one ready-made case under their own heels'). The etymology is even posed as a test-question: (座下無席帽)，(案邊無胥吏)，(階下無荊條竹根)，(為甚麼祖師語言喚作公案)？ ('no magistrate's cap on the seat, no clerks by the desk, no switches below the steps — why are the patriarchs' words called public cases?', 聚雲吹萬真禪師語錄). The texts gloss the two graphs by the legal-record figure and add nothing beyond it, and neither does this entry.
Senses.Note: Consistent across three independent Zen witnesses spanning Song to Yuan (碧巖錄序; 無門關 self-preface; 天目中峰廣錄), all foregrounding the legal-record sense. No master bends the term to a private meaning, so a single corpus-wide sense. Zen-scoped counts: (公案) 3,800x in 363 allowlist texts. Attested collocations: (現成公案) ('a ready-made case') 382x/154 texts; (古人公案) ('the old men's public cases') 138x/73; (一則公案) ('one case', counted with the measure word 則) 84x/57; the corpus's own tally of the case-literature, (千七百則公案) ('the seventeen hundred cases') 64x/45 (e.g. 凡一千七百則公案 'in all one thousand seven hundred cases', 天目中峰廣錄 0731a13); (舉公案) ('raising a public case') 22x/20; (看公案) ('looking at public cases') 16x/9 (諸方愛教人看公案 'everywhere they love to set people looking at public cases', 古尊宿語錄 C077n1710 0847a18); (公案未圓) ('the case not yet rounded off') 17x/15.
